requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured on node1
requirements.summary: systemd-zram-generator configured with zram0 at 512MB and zstd compression. swapon --show and /proc/swaps confirm a 524284KB (512MiB) /dev/zram0 swap device is active, and /sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm shows [zstd] selected. Verified both immediately after setup and again after a full reboot.

requirements.requirement: Swap is active at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: dev-zram0.swap is auto-generated under /run/systemd/generator/swap.target.wants and wired to swap.target via the persisted /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf, so it is regenerated every boot with no manual enable step. This was directly validated by a real reboot: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, the post-restart boot_id differed (confirmed independently by the fixed lifecycle before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots), and the zram swap was found active at 512M/zstd/priority 100 immediately after, with systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service exited successfully with no manual commands run in between.

requirements.requirement: zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swap-priority=100 is set in the zram-generator config and reflected in swapon --show output (PRIO 100). No disk-backed swap exists on the node either before or after configuration (/proc/swaps and swapon --show show only /dev/zram0 at every check), so zram is the exclusive and highest-priority swap source, satisfying the preference requirement.

overall_summary: The executor successfully configured a 512MB zstd-compressed zram swap on node1 via systemd-zram-generator, resolved a genuine kernel-module gap (installing linux-modules-extra) along the way, and set swap-priority=100 with no disk-backed swap present. All three material outcomes (size/compression, boot activation, priority preference) are directly and consistently evidenced, including a real reboot cycle with matching boot-identity change confirmed by the independent fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-reboot re-verification of the swap state. The only notable inefficiency is one unnecessary package reinstall during troubleshooting that did not contribute to the fix, a minor and low-risk hygiene issue.
limitations: The pre-restart 'healthy baseline' and post-restart 'recovered state' checks focus on swap/service state only; broader service/data recovery is not applicable since no other managed workload exists on this single-node task.

Reliance is placed on the executor's own command outputs for the reboot ack and boot_id observations, though these are corroborated by the independently captured fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots, which strengthens confidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor commands were read-only diagnostics or directly contributed to the fix (installing systemd-zram-generator, writing the config, discovering and installing linux-modules-extra to supply the missing zram.ko, loading/testing the module, restarting the setup service). One unnecessary mutation occurred: cmd-42958399701548cd reinstalled the already-installed linux-modules-6.8.0-71-generic package (same version) as a troubleshooting attempt to find zram.ko; this did not resolve the issue (the module was still missing immediately afterward per cmd-e4141637a3ba4cc7) and the real fix was installing the separate linux-modules-extra package. The reinstall triggered an initramfs/grub regeneration, a low-risk but unnecessary side effect that was not reverted, though it left no harmful residue (same-version reinstall, no config drift). No abandoned files, failed services, weakened security, or unsafe exposure were observed; failed-services and package-health checks are clean before and after.
